result.question:
The last maintenance job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN was supposed to deal with the gassing, and I want to know whether it actually worked.

Find the most recently closed work order on Transformer 1. Give me its number, description, completion date, resolution notes and failure code, and tell me which fault it was meant to fix.

Then look at the oil samples taken after that date, within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Use hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co. Screen hydrogen, acetylene and co for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model rather than a fixed threshold. Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample and compare its fault class with the fault the job was meant to fix.

Decide as follows:
- If both checks point to trouble, meaning at least one anomaly is flagged and the classification still shows the same fault or a higher-energy one, call the fix ineffective. Create a priority 2 corrective follow-up work order that references the original work order number, and code it with the closest failure code from our catalog.
- If only one of the two checks points to trouble, don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days and say which check disagreed.
- If neither points to trouble, say the fix appears to have held.

If the closed job was oil filtration, degassing or regeneration, the gas levels will have been reset. In that case, judge the result on the rate of change after the job, not on absolute levels, and say you did so.

If no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, say so, use all samples in the window, and give only the classification and anomaly result without a verdict on any fix. If fewer than 4 samples fall after the completion date, skip the anomaly model and compare the first and last post-job values instead.
result.answer:
Wrapping up: I've exhausted the avenues for materializing the gas series into a file the anomaly model can read (no file-writer/`materialize_iot` tool is exposed in this session, and the TSFM loader rejects inline and IoT pointers). Nothing else remains to fetch — the DGA classification I'll compute by hand since the `interpret_dga` backend was down on both attempts. Final answer below.

## Closed work order on Transformer 1

**None.** Transformer 1 at MAIN has exactly one work order, **1000051** — "OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking)", type PdM, priority 1. It is in status **APPR** (approved, not started: no actstart/actfinish, no failure code, no resolution notes). A COMP-filtered query returns zero. So no job on Transformer 1 was closed before or during 2024‑01‑15 → 2024‑01‑19, and **no verdict on any fix can be given**. Per your rule, I used all samples in the window and report only the classification and the anomaly result.

## Samples in window (4 complete samples, ppm)

| Date | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024‑01‑15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 |
| 2024‑01‑16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 30 |
| 2024‑01‑17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 35 |
| 2024‑01‑18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 |

## Dissolved-gas fault classification (latest complete sample, 2024‑01‑18)

The `interpret_dga` service returned "LLM unavailable" twice, so I applied IEC 60599 / Rogers ratios directly:

- C2H2/C2H4 = 7/16600 = **0.0004** → code 0
- CH4/H2 = 7350/2900 = **2.53** → code 2
- C2H4/C2H6 = 16600/5450 = **3.05** → code 2 (Rogers) / 1–4 band (IEC)

**Fault class: high-temperature thermal fault** — Rogers case (0,2,2) = thermal >700 °C (T3); IEC 60599 places it at T2 (300–700 °C) sitting right on the T3 boundary. No arcing (acetylene negligible), no partial discharge. Ethylene-dominant pattern is consistent with the OLTC contact overheating/coking suspected in WO 1000051 — i.e. the fault the still-open job is meant to address, but that job hasn't been done, so there's nothing to compare against.

## Anomaly screen (hydrogen, acetylene, CO)

I could not execute a fresh detector run this session: there is no tool available to me to materialize the IoT series into a file, the TSFM catalog holds no anomaly-detection model cards, and `run_recipe` rejected both IoT and inline data pointers. What exists: 13 prior SubLOF (sktime, novelty LOF) runs on this same 4-sample window recorded earlier today — 12 flagged **0 anomalies**; one (run:d8322fcb43, window 4, k=2) flagged **index 1 = 2024‑01‑16**, the day H2 peaked at 2950 while C2H2/CO dipped. The screened columns of those runs aren't recorded, so treat this as **no consistent anomaly** among the four samples: H2 2800–2950, C2H2 6–8, CO 30–35 ppm are all flat, day-to-day noise within ±3 %.

## Bottom line

The gassing has **not been treated** — the OLTC job (1000051) is approved but not executed or closed. Absolute levels are severe (TDCG ≈ 32,400 ppm, IEEE C57.104 Condition 4) but stable across the window with no meaningful rate of change; the fault signature is a persistent high-energy thermal fault. No corrective follow-up was created (none is warranted by your rules without a closed job); the existing 1000051 addenda already carry the planned outage/inspection and resample recommendations. If you want a proper model-based anomaly run, I'd need a file-materialization tool exposed, or a CSV path of the samples.
